competencies.text: Use chemical equations for photosynthesis and respiration.
Describe metabolic reactions in body cells and their significance.

days.title: Balancing Chemical Equations
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to read, write, and balance chemical equations, including the equations for photosynthesis and cellular respiration, and describe metabolic reactions in body cells.

🧪 What Is a Chemical Equation?

A chemical equation is a symbolic representation of a chemical reaction. It uses chemical formulas to show what reacts and what forms.

Reactants → Products

Example:

2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O

This says: two molecules of hydrogen gas react with one molecule of oxygen gas to produce two molecules of water.

📐 Parts of an Equation

PartMeaningExample
Chemical formulaThe substance involvedH₂O, CO₂, C₆H₁₂O₆
CoefficientNumber of molecules (whole number in front)The
in 2H₂OSubscriptNumber of atoms of an element in a moleculeThe

Reactants → ProductsState symbols (optional)(s) solid, (l) liquid, (g) gas, (aq) aqueousNaCl(aq)

⚖️ Law of Conservation of Mass

Atoms are neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction. This means: the number of each type of atom must be the same on both sides of the equation.

If it isn't, the equation is unbalanced and needs coefficients to fix it.

🔧 How to Balance an Equation

  1. Write the unbalanced (skeleton) equation.
  2. Count atoms of each element on both sides.
  3. Add coefficients (never change subscripts!) to balance one element at a time.
  4. Recount — check that all atoms are equal.
  5. Simplify coefficients to the smallest whole-number ratio if possible.

Example — combustion of methane:

CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O

🌿 Photosynthesis — The Green Equation

Plants use sunlight to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen:

6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light energy → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂

  • Reactants: 6 CO₂ + 6 H₂O + light
  • Products: 1 glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) + 6 oxygen (O₂)
  • Location: Chloroplasts in plant cells
  • Importance: Produces the oxygen we breathe and the food we eat.

💨 Cellular Respiration — The Body's Engine

Cells break down glucose using oxygen to release energy:

C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + energy (ATP)

  • Reactants: glucose + oxygen
  • Products: carbon dioxide + water + energy
  • Location: Mitochondria in cells
  • Importance: Provides ATP — the energy currency your body runs on.

🔗 Photosynthesis + Respiration = A Cycle

Notice — photosynthesis and respiration are opposite reactions:

  • Photosynthesis uses CO₂ + H₂O and produces glucose + O₂.
  • Respiration uses glucose + O₂ and produces CO₂ + H₂O.

Together, they form the carbon-oxygen cycle that keeps life on Earth in balance.

🧬 Metabolic Reactions in Body Cells

  • Catabolism: Breaking down larger molecules (e.g., glucose) to release energy.
  • Anabolism: Building larger molecules (e.g., proteins from amino acids) using energy.
  • Examples: Digestion, protein synthesis, DNA replication, muscle contraction.
  • Significance: All bodily functions — from breathing to thinking — depend on metabolic reactions.

📌 Quick Check

  • Why must equations be balanced? (Answer: conservation of mass)
  • What are the products of photosynthesis? (Answer: glucose and oxygen)
  • What is ATP? (Answer: the energy currency produced by respiration)

days.title: Match Game — Equation Components
days.content:
🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each equation term or reaction to its correct description. There are 8 pairs and unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

match.right: Substance that reacts on the left side of the arrow
Substance formed on the right side of the arrow
Whole number placed in front of a formula to balance the equation
Atoms are neither created nor destroyed in a reaction

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Reactions in Cells
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best reasoning. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: 🌿 A plant is placed in a sealed transparent container with a CO₂ sensor. After a sunny day, the CO₂ level drops. Why?

choices.label: A) The plant is producing CO₂ at night
B) The plant is absorbing CO₂ for photosynthesis, using it to make glucose and releasing O₂
C) The container is leaking CO₂
D) CO₂ evaporates in the sun

scenario.text: 🏃 You sprint for 100 meters and start breathing heavily. Which reaction is happening faster in your muscles?

choices.label: B) Cellular respiration — breaking down glucose with oxygen to release ATP energy
C) Combustion of glucose with flames

scenario.text: ⚖️ You balance the equation: __ H₂ + O₂ → __ H₂O. What coefficients make it balanced?

choices.label: B) 2 in front of H₂ and 2 in front of H₂O

scenario.text: 🌍 Why are photosynthesis and respiration considered 'opposite reactions'?

choices.label: A) Their reactants and products are reversed
B) They happen in the same organelle

scenario.text: 🍔 After eating rice, your body breaks down the starch into glucose. This is an example of:

choices.label: B) Catabolism — breaking down larger molecules to release energy

days.title: Formative Check — Escape the Equation Lab
days.content:
🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Equation Lab

You have 3 lives and 6 keys to unlock. You need 75% (5 of 6) to pass. Take your time — read every option carefully.

escape.text: What does the arrow (→) in a chemical equation mean?
Why must a chemical equation be balanced?

choices.label: A) Because of the Law of Conservation of Mass — atoms are neither created nor destroyed
B) To make it look nicer

escape.text: Which equation correctly represents cellular respiration?
Where in the cell does cellular respiration mainly occur?
What does ATP provide to a cell?
